messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: GPU pool 'inference-eu' queue growing > 5000; autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops in 10m but hit cap. Severity: P1. @Mike (oncall) paged :rotating_light:

Mike (oncall): Seeing a surge in request rate. Latency spikes on hosted API, errors 503s reported by load- balancer. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/example/alerts/1725

Anya (infra): Oncall logs: autoscaler log shows 'scale_up rejected - project quota limit reached' and "allocation failed: fragments_only" for MIG shapes. Copying snippets:
```
2024-05-12T11:02:03Z | autoscaler | attemptScaleUp req=12 -> rejected: quota_exhausted
2024-05-12T11:04:10Z | scheduler  | placement failed: leftover_slots: [1g-0.25mig, 0.5g], reason: fragmentation
2024-05-12T11:05:22Z | queuemgr   | inflight: 5600, pending: 4200, avg_wait: 18s
```

Devon (scheduler): This looks like a twofold problem: (1) cluster-level GPU quota prevents more nodes, (2) existing hosts are fragmented because many jobs were placed using small MIG slices (0.25 / 0.5) leaving unusable remainders. Batching/backfill can't pack them.

Priya (CS): We have customer reports from a few high-traffic customers (org: synthmedia, adprox) about 5-15s extra latency and rate-limited calls failing. They're on support tier 2. Need ETA for mitigation.

Mike (oncall): Current impact: API error rate up ~8% for text-gen endpoints; embeddings degraded for large-batch jobs. Mitigation options?

Anya (infra): Short-term: 1) temporarily increase per-org GPU cap if available (requires approver). 2) Trigger emergency surge pool activation (if enabled) to add 6xA100 nodes in eu-region. 3) Manual eviction of low-priority jobs to defrag and free contiguous MIG slots.

Devon (scheduler): Eviction plan: identify pods with priority "batch-low" and age < 1h and preempt them. Command: ```./tools/evict --pool inference-eu --filter 'priority=batch-low' --dry-run``` Running dry-run now to show candidates.

SRE-Bot: Dry-run results: 412 candidates (est free slices: 8 x full-GPU equivalents if evicted). No critical customers in that set.

Mike (oncall): Mike to request surge pool activation and approval for quota bump. @Anya can you start eviction after approval? I'll open an incident ticket and notify CS.

Anya (infra): Requesting quota bump: submitted form to cloud-ops with "urgent-autoscale-bump" tag. If approved, nodes available ~9-12 min. Meanwhile starting eviction now to reclaim some capacity. Executing: ```./tools/evict --pool inference-eu --filter 'priority=batch-low' --confirm --limit 250```

Devon (scheduler): Eviction in flight: 250 pods terminated and rescheduled. Observed immediate reclaim: 3.25 full GPUs worth of spans — but still fragmented. Trying a targeted coalesce: scheduling controller attempting to migrate a few small inference instances to combine slices. That requires draining 2 hosts temporarily: `kubectl drain host-aaa --ignore-daemonsets` (will cause a short interruption on those tenants).

Priya (CS): Please mark the affected customers and message them: synthmedia and adprox flagged. Draft: "We're experiencing degraded inference performance due to GPU placement congestion; mitigation in progress. We'll update within 30 minutes."

SRE-Bot: Cloud approval response: quota bump denied (policy: manual review needed). Surge pool activation: activation queued but dependent on capacity reservation; estimate 18-22 min to become effective.

Mike (oncall): Given quota denial and surge lag, proceed with more aggressive defrag: manual repack/evacuate smaller MIG slices (0.25/0.5) into newly freed bigger slots. Devon, coordinate migration windows.

Devon (scheduler): Running repack plan: 1) pause new admissions for 5m, 2) migrate 12 medium pods onto 4 hosts, 3) evict low-priority slices from 6 hosts, 4) uncordon sequentially. Commands: 
```
./ctl admission pause --pool inference-eu --duration 5m
./ctl repack --pool inference-eu --strategy greedy --targets 6
```

Anya (infra): Admission paused. Repack reported success on 4 hosts; reclaimed two contiguous full-GPU slots. Queue pending dropped from 4200 -> 3100 in 12m, avg wait now 10s. 

Priya (CS): Notifying customers: sent update to synthmedia/adprox. PR copy in #customer-updates. They replied: "Thanks, we can ramp down noncritical jobs. Keep us posted."

SRE-Bot: Autoscaler attempted one more scale after repack but still rejected due to global project quota. Also detected placement thrash: repeated small migrations causing CPU pressure on nodes; taking 3% request error increase briefly.

Mike (oncall): Action items now:
- Continue repack and watch queue numbers (Devon + Anya)
- CS: keep customers updated (Priya)
- If surge pool activates, hold off further evictions to let new nodes absorb load (Mike)
- Post-incident: review MIG size policy and autoscaler quotas (owners: Devon, Anya)

Devon (scheduler): Repack now moved an additional 8 pods, reclaimed 1.5 GPUs. Pending 2400 -> 1650 in 25m since start. Latency returning toward baseline for 95th pct. But binpacking fragmentation remains in some racks due to heterogeneous MIG sizes (0.25 vs 0.75). Propose short-term policy: prefer uniform MIG shapes for new allocations (0.5 or full) until we refactor allocator.

Anya (infra): Surge pool activation: 6 nodes live in eu in 20m. Autoscaler now able to place new allocs. After surge: pending queue immediate drop to 300 and avg wait ~1.8s. Errors down to baseline.

Priya (CS): Customer synthmedia confirms degraded window closed; they're seeing baseline times now. Adprox still reports occasional throttling — looks like a token bucket refill issue on their side.

SRE-Bot: Incident status: Mitigated (service restored). Root-cause summary: scheduler fragmentation + conservative project GPU quotas prevented autoscaler from scaling beyond cluster capacity, resulting in queue growth and throttling.

Mike (oncall): Handoff to next oncall: @Devon you'll own follow-up RCA and quota appeals. @Anya own remediation: audit MIG size mix + temporary policy to prefer 0.5/full shapes. Priya continue customer comms for any lingering cases. I'll update the incident ticket and run blameless postmortem template.

Devon (scheduler): Acknowledged. Initial RCA notes saved to incident: https://incidents.redwood/1725012345/notes. Start time 2024-05-12T11:01Z, mitigation 2024-05-12T11:45Z, recovery 2024-05-12T11:55Z.

Anya (infra): Follow-ups: 1) request permanent quota increase for svc-account autoscaler/infra 2) add admission policy to favor compatible MIG sizes 3) add autoscaler fallback to temporarily relax per-project caps in emergency (audit trail required). Placing tasks in infra backlog.

Priya (CS): Closing note to customers: "All systems recovered. We performed targeted evacuations and temporary capacity activation. We're following up with an RCA and action plan to prevent recurrence."

SRE-Bot: Incident closed as mitigated; please attach postmortem within 72h.

Mike (oncall): Thanks team. I'll file the postmortem and schedule a 1hr blameless review tomorrow.
